title: ROS 2 Operations: Launch & Parameter Composition, Deterministic rosbag2 Recording/Replay & Simulator Integration (Gazebo / MuJoCo)

blocks.x: This is the final bridge module in the Track 06 Tier 2 ladder before Step 2.7 (`06-robotics.T2.07`). In `06-robotics.T2.06a`, you learned how individual ROS 2 nodes, `tf2` trees, and `ros2_control` interfaces operate. In a real robotics lab, you never start 15 terminals by hand or test an untested Cartesian impedance controller directly on a $48\text{ V}$ metal arm! You orchestrate the entire stack from a declarative **Python `LaunchDescription` + YAML parameter file** (with intra-process **Component Composition** for zero-copy image/point-cloud passing), record and deterministically replay multi-topic **`rosbag2` (`MCAP`)** logs using simulated time (`use_sim_time: true` + `--clock`) to debug estimators and train imitation-learning policies (`Track 06 Tier 3`), and close the $1\text{ kHz}$ **`ros2_control` $\leftrightarrow$ Physics Simulator (`MuJoCo` / `Gazebo Harmonic`)** loop so your exact C++ controller runs identically in simulation and on physical hardware. Already know this? Take the Skip test or the Ladder Gate test in section 7 first.
Three operational workflows turn a collection of ROS 2 nodes into a reproducible robotics testbed:

items.x: **Launch Files, Parameters & Intra-Process Composition (`Zero-Copy`):** A **`LaunchDescription`** (`arm_bringup.launch.py`) is the conductor's score: it parses your `Xacro` $\to$ `URDF`, loads gain tables from `controllers.yaml`, spawns `robot_state_publisher` and `controller_manager`, and sets `use_sim_time` across every node simultaneously. Even better, when a camera node and a visual detector node are loaded as `ComposableNode` plugins inside a single `ComposableNodeContainer` process with `use_intra_process_comms=True`, ROS 2 passes a `std::unique_ptr<Image>` memory pointer directly between them in $< 1\ \mu\text{s}$ instead of copying megabytes over DDS sockets!

**`rosbag2` (`MCAP`) Recording & Deterministic Replay:** Think of **`rosbag2`** as a flight-data black box (`ros2 bag record -s mcap -a`). When you record `/joint_states`, `/tf`, and `/camera/image_raw` into an indexed **MCAP** file (`Foxglove` / `Rerun` standard), every message is stored with its exact recording timestamp. When you replay that bag offline with `ros2 bag play my_run.mcap --clock` and set `use_sim_time:=true` on your Kalman filter or SLAM node, `rosbag2` broadcasts a virtual `/clock` topic that drives all ROS timers deterministically—letting you replay a $10\text{ s}$ collision or slip event at $0.1\times$ or $10\times$ real-time speed and get bit-identical outputs on every run!

**How ROS 2 Connects to `MuJoCo` & `Gazebo Harmonic` (`The Closed-Loop Simulator Bridge`):** A physics simulator is not just a 3D viewer—it replaces the physical motors and encoders underneath `ros2_control`! On every physics step $\Delta t_{\text{sim}} = 1\text{ ms}$:
The simulator steps rigid-body dynamics $M(q)\ddot{q} + C(q,\dot{q})\dot{q} + g(q) = \tau_{\text{cmd}}$ forward by $\Delta t_{\text{sim}}$ and publishes the simulated timestamp onto `/clock`.

The simulator plugin (`gz_ros2_control` in Gazebo Harmonic or `mujoco_ros2_control` in MuJoCo) copies simulated joint positions, velocities, and efforts $(q, \dot{q}, \tau)$ into `ros2_control`'s `SystemInterface::read()` **`state_interfaces`**.

`controller_manager::update()` runs your **exact same** `joint_state_broadcaster` (which publishes `/joint_states` $\to$ `robot_state_publisher` $\to$ `/tf`) and your **exact same** Cartesian impedance or trajectory controller, writing desired torques $\tau_{\text{cmd}}$ into **`command_interfaces`**.
`SystemInterface::write()` writes $\tau_{\text{cmd}}$ into `mjData->ctrl` (MuJoCo) or joint force buffers (Gazebo) for the next physics step!
**Launch Parameter Resolution, Simulated Clock (`use_sim_time`) & Intra-Process Pointer Transfer:**

**Simulated Time Rule:** When parameter `use_sim_time == True`, `Node::now()` ignores the OS wall clock (`CLOCK_REALTIME`) and returns the latest timestamp received on `/clock` (`rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock`). If `/clock` advances in discrete steps of $\Delta t_{\text{sim}}$, a ROS timer with period $T_{\text{timer}}$ fires deterministically every $K = \lceil T_{\text{timer}} / \Delta t_{\text{sim}} \rceil$ simulation steps regardless of CPU load.

**Intra-Process vs. Inter-Process Bandwidth Savings:** Passing a message of size $B_{\text{msg}}$ bytes at frequency $f_{\text{pub}}$ across $N_{\text{sub}}$ intra-process `ComposableNode` subscribers via `unique_ptr` ownership transfer copies $0\text{ bytes}$ of payload (only an $8\text{-byte}$ pointer), saving serialized memory bandwidth:
**`rosbag2` (`MCAP`) Storage Throughput, Ring-Buffer Sizing & Replay Scaling:**

**Write Throughput & Storage Size:** Recording $M$ topics with message sizes $B_m$ (plus per-message MCAP index/timestamp overhead $B_{\text{meta}} \approx 32\text{ B}$) at frequencies $f_m$ ($\text{Hz}$) over duration $T_{\text{rec}}$ ($\text{s}$) with compression ratio $c \in (0, 1]$ ($c=1$ uncompressed) requires sustained disk write rate $R_{\text{disk}}$ and file size $S_{\text{bag}}$:

blocks.tex: R_{\text{disk}} = c \sum_{m=1}^{M} f_m (B_m + B_{\text{meta}}), \qquad S_{\text{bag}} = R_{\text{disk}} \cdot T_{\text{rec}}

items.x: **Replay Rate Scaling (`--rate r`):** Playing back a bag recorded at interval $\Delta t_{\text{rec}} = t_{k+1} - t_k$ with playback rate factor $r > 0$ schedules wall-clock sleep $\Delta t_{\text{wall}} = \Delta t_{\text{rec}} / r$ while publishing the **original** message timestamps $t_k$ on `/clock`, preserving exact numerical derivatives $\frac{x(t_{k+1}) - x(t_k)}{t_{k+1} - t_k}$ at any playback speed!
**Closed-Loop Simulator $\leftrightarrow$ `ros2_control` Synchronization Contract:**

Let the physics engine step at frequency $f_{\text{sim}} = 1 / \Delta t_{\text{sim}}$ (e.g., $1000\text{ Hz}$) and the `ros2_control` `controller_manager` run at $f_{\text{ctrl}} = f_{\text{sim}} / D$ for integer decimation $D \ge 1$.
On simulation step $k$:

blocks.x: **Predict first (before you run it):** Commit to four numbers before the code runs. (1) With the three topics at $1\text{ kHz}$/$128\text{ B}$, $200\text{ Hz}$/$96\text{ B}$ and $30\text{ Hz}$/$150{,}000\text{ B}$, $32\text{ B}$ of metadata per message and `zstd` at $c = 0.40$, what sustained disk rate and what $10$-minute file size do you expect? (2) Does the estimated $\dot{q}$ change when the same bag is replayed at `--rate 4.0` instead of `--rate 0.5`? (3) After $20$ steps of $1\text{ ms}$ with $k_p = 25.0$, $k_d = 2.5$, $J = 0.05$ and $b = 0.20$, roughly how far has the joint moved? Two tells: a derivative that changes with the playback rate means wall-clock time leaked into the estimate, and a file size that ignores the $32\text{ B}$ metadata is short by exactly $f_m \cdot 32$ bytes per second on every topic.

Simulate a complete ROS 2 operational workflow in Python: (1) compute the `rosbag2` MCAP write throughput and 10-minute file size for a robot recording $1\text{ kHz}$ `/joint_states` ($128\text{ B}$), $200\text{ Hz}$ `/imu/data` ($96\text{ B}$), and $30\text{ Hz}$ `/camera/depth` ($150{,}000\text{ B}$) with `zstd` compression ($c = 0.40$), (2) verify deterministic `--rate 4.0` replay derivative invariance using `/clock` timestamps, and (3) run a 20-step closed-loop `MuJoCo / Gazebo` $\leftrightarrow$ `ros2_control` (`read -> update -> write`) + `robot_state_publisher` (`/joint_states` $\to$ `/tf`) simulation loop.

blocks.text:
import math

# 1. rosbag2 MCAP storage & disk throughput budget (B_meta = 32 B per message, zstd compression c = 0.40):
topics = [
    ("/joint_states", 1000.0, 128),
    ("/imu/data",      200.0,  96),
    ("/camera/depth",   30.0, 150_000),
]
B_meta = 32
c_zstd = 0.40
raw_rate_bps = sum(f * (b + B_meta) for _, f, b in topics)
disk_rate_mbs = (c_zstd * raw_rate_bps) / 1e6
bag_size_10min_mb = disk_rate_mbs * 600.0
assert math.isclose(raw_rate_bps, 160_000.0 + 25_600.0 + 4_500_960.0, rel_tol=1e-9)
assert math.isclose(disk_rate_mbs, 1.874624, rel_tol=1e-6)

# 2. Deterministic rosbag2 replay with --clock at rate r = 0.5x vs r = 4.0x:
bag_msgs = [(10.000, 0.50), (10.002, 0.54)]  # (sim_time_s, q_rad)
for rate in [0.5, 1.0, 4.0]:
    dt_wall = (bag_msgs[1][0] - bag_msgs[0][0]) / rate
    dt_sim_clock = bag_msgs[1][0] - bag_msgs[0][0]  # Estimator uses /clock (dt_sim_clock), NOT dt_wall!
    dq_est = (bag_msgs[1][1] - bag_msgs[0][1]) / dt_sim_clock
    assert math.isclose(dq_est, 20.0, rel_tol=1e-9)  # Identical 20.0 rad/s at every playback rate!

# 3. Closed-loop Simulator (MuJoCo/Gazebo) <-> ros2_control (read/update/write) + /joint_states -> /tf:
q_sim, dq_sim = 0.0, 0.0
inertia, damping, dt_sim = 0.05, 0.20, 0.001
q_target, kp, kd = 1.0, 25.0, 2.5
link_len = 0.30

for step in range(20):
    # (a) Simulator plugin SystemInterface::read() exports state_interfaces
    q_state, dq_state = q_sim, dq_sim
    # (b) controller_manager::update() -> PD effort controller + JointStateBroadcaster
    tau_cmd = kp * (q_target - q_state) - kd * dq_state
    # (c) robot_state_publisher computes /tf from /joint_states and URDF link length:
    tf_tip_x, tf_tip_y = link_len * math.cos(q_state), link_len * math.sin(q_state)
    # (d) Simulator plugin SystemInterface::write() applies tau_cmd to physics step:
    ddq = (tau_cmd - damping * dq_sim) / inertia
    dq_sim += ddq * dt_sim
    q_sim += dq_sim * dt_sim

assert q_sim > 0.05 and math.isclose(tf_tip_x**2 + tf_tip_y**2, link_len**2, rel_tol=1e-9)
print(f"disk_rate={disk_rate_mbs:.3f} MB/s, bag_10m={bag_size_10min_mb:.1f} MB, q_sim(20ms)={q_sim:.4f} rad")
disk_rate=1.875 MB/s, bag_10m=1124.8 MB, q_sim(20ms)=0.0752 rad

Edit it, then run the tests the way CI does:

The tests are behavioural: a $2.5$-step timer must wait $3$ (rounding and flooring both drift), an exact multiple must not round up from float error, the $0.40$ `zstd` budget must be $1.874624\text{ MB/s}$ and $1124.7744\text{ MB}$ for ten minutes, the $32\text{ B}$ per-message index must show as $0.128 \to 0.160\text{ MB/s}$ on one joint-state topic, compression must scale the rate rather than the size, the replay derivative must stay $20\text{ rad/s}$ at $0.25\times$, $1\times$ and $4\times$, and $1000/300$ must **raise** instead of becoming $3$. The transfer suite records the plant's own $20\text{ B}$ telemetry frame at $1\text{ kHz}$ for a minute and requires the budget to be a few megabytes, shows the $32\text{ B}$ metadata multiplying that frame's rate, puts a $250\text{ Hz}$ task on the plant's $1\text{ kHz}$ clock (four ticks apart, $250$ firings in a $1000$-tick run), and takes the figure-8 tip velocity off the plant's recorded stamps at $1\times$ and $4\times$ so the two must agree to $10^{-15}$. Four planted faults - `timer_rounds`, `disk_ignores_meta`, `replay_assumed_dt`, `decimation_rounds` - each fail the test named for them.

items.x: **The recording budget is a sum of rates, each with its metadata.** $500 \times (168 + 32) = 100{,}000\ \text{B/s}$ and $20 \times (99{,}968 + 32) = 2{,}000{,}000\ \text{B/s}$, so $R_{\text{disk}} = 2{,}100{,}000/10^6 = 2.10\ \text{MB/s}$ at $c = 1.0$. Adding the $32\ \text{B}$ once per topic instead of once per message is the classic slip: it would give $2.0834\ \text{MB/s}$.

**Size and replay are two different multiplications.** $S_{\text{bag}} = R_{\text{disk}} T_{\text{rec}} = 2.10 \times 100 = 210.0\ \text{MB}$, while the replay only divides time: $T_{\text{wall}} = 100/2.5 = 40.0\ \text{s}$. The bag does not shrink because you played it faster.

**Simulated time is what makes replay deterministic.** $\dot{q}$ is $(q_b - q_a)/(t_b - t_a)$ on the message stamps - $20\ \text{rad/s}$ at $0.5\times$, $1\times$ and $4\times$ - so a derivative that changes with `--rate` proves wall-clock time leaked into the estimator. And a timer of $2.5$ simulation steps must fire on step $3$: `ceil`, and at least one step.

**Decimation is exact or refused.** $1000/250 = 4$ is a whole number; $1000/300 = 3.33$ is not, and returning $3$ silently runs the controller at $300\ \text{Hz}$ while claiming $2\bar{3}\ \text{Hz}$ - so raise instead.

**What the suite refuses.** `timer_steps` refuses a non-positive timer period or simulation step, `wall_delay_s` refuses a non-positive replay rate, `replay_derivative` refuses two samples on the same stamp, and `control_decimation` refuses a zero controller rate or a ratio that is not a whole number - each raises `ValueError`.

items.x: **Inject:** run `ros2 bag play arm_test_bag --rate 2.5` and omit the `--clock` flag, leaving `robot_state_publisher` and the estimator on simulated time.

**Symptom:** the bag reports $40.0\text{ s}$ of wall-clock playback, but every node's `now()` stays at $0$ simulation seconds; timers that should fire every $K = \lceil 1\text{ ms}/1\text{ ms} \rceil = 1$ step never fire, and `tf2` throws `Lookup would require extrapolation` because it holds a $12\text{ s}$ sim-time transform while a wall-clock node queries at $1.7 \times 10^9\text{ s}$.

**Diagnose:** the file plays and `/joint_states` messages exist, so the bag, the rate factor and the MCAP index are all healthy; a frozen `now()` on a bag that is visibly advancing can only be a missing `/clock` publisher, not a decimation or timer-period error.

**Fix:** add `--clock`, then prove it by `ros2 topic hz /clock` reporting $1\text{ kHz}$ and `ros2 topic echo /clock` advancing $0.001\text{ s}$ per message, with the estimator's $\dot{q}$ back at $20\text{ rad/s}$ at $0.25\times$, $1\times$ and $4\times$.

rows: Nodes freeze or timers never fire when replaying a `rosbag2` with `use_sim_time:=true`
Forgot to pass the `--clock` flag to `ros2 bag play`, so no `/clock` messages are published.
Always run `ros2 bag play <bag> --clock` whenever downstream nodes have `use_sim_time:=true`.
`tf2` throws `Lookup would require extrapolation into the past` during simulation or bag replay

Mixed wall-clock nodes (`use_sim_time:=false`) with simulated-clock nodes (`use_sim_time:=true`), stamping `/tf` at $t = 12text{ s}$ (sim time) while querying at $t = 1.7 times 10^9text{ s}$ (Unix epoch time).
Set `use_sim_time: true` globally in your `LaunchDescription` across **all** nodes (`robot_state_publisher`, `rviz2`, controllers, estimators).
Simulated robot arm collapses to the floor as soon as `Gazebo` or `MuJoCo` starts
Spawned the robot model before loading and activating `joint_state_broadcaster` and the position/impedance controller in `controller_manager`.
Use `RegisterEventHandler(OnProcessExit(...))` in your launch file to spawn `joint_state_broadcaster` and your active controller immediately as the simulator `controller_manager` comes online.
